series.low-poly.name: Low poly
series.low-poly.title: Low Poly 3D Asset Packs
series.low-poly.seoTitle: Low Poly 3D Asset Packs for Unity, Godot & Unreal
series.low-poly.blurb: Modular low poly cities, traffic, villages, schools, SWAT teams and more, all on one palette texture, one scale and one 8 m grid.
series.low-poly.long: The core HanX Games series: stylized low poly 3D models built to snap together. Every pack shares a single 1024×1024 palette texture and one material, so an entire city scene batches into a single draw call. Made for mobile games, prototypes, city builders, driving games, simulators and tactical shooters.
series.3d-pixel.name: 3D pixel
series.3d-pixel.title: 3D Pixel Art Asset Packs
series.3d-pixel.seoTitle: 3D Pixel Art Asset Packs: Voxel-Style Models for Games
series.3d-pixel.blurb: Crunchy pixel textures on clean 3D shapes: dungeons, medieval towns, farms, interiors, RPG items and a SWAT squad.
series.3d-pixel.long: 3D pixel art (also called HD-2D or pixel-textured low poly) gives you the charm of retro sprites with real 3D lighting and cameras. Each HanX 3D Pixel pack uses point-filtered pixel textures at one texel density, so dungeons, towns and props from different packs sit together.

engine.unity.title: Low Poly 3D Assets for Unity
engine.unity.how: Drag the FBX or GLB files into your Assets folder, assign the shared palette material once and drop prefabs into your scene. Works with URP, HDRP and the Built-in pipeline.
engine.unity.s1: Unzip the pack and drag the FBX files into your Assets folder. GLB works too with Unity’s glTFast package.
engine.unity.s2: Create one material from the included palette texture (URP Lit, HDRP Lit or Standard) and assign it to every model.
engine.unity.s3: Drag the models into your scene and save the ones you reuse as prefabs. They are already at real-world scale.
engine.unity.s4: Mark props that never move as Static so Unity batches them into a handful of draw calls.
engine.godot.title: Low Poly 3D Assets for Godot 4
engine.godot.how: Godot 4 imports GLB natively: copy the files into res://, double-click to create inherited scenes and you are done. One material keeps mobile and web exports fast.
engine.godot.s1: Copy the GLB files anywhere inside your project folder (res://). Godot 4 imports them automatically.
engine.godot.s2: Drag a GLB into your scene, or double-click it and choose New Inherited Scene to make a reusable scene.
engine.godot.s3: Every model uses the same small palette texture: extract the material once in Advanced Import Settings and reuse it everywhere.
engine.godot.s4: For repeated props such as trees, fences or lamps, use a MultiMeshInstance3D to keep mobile and web exports fast.
engine.unreal.title: Low Poly 3D Assets for Unreal Engine 5
engine.unreal.how: Import the FBX files with Combine Meshes off, create one material instance from the palette texture and reuse it for every mesh. Nanite is not needed, the models are already tiny.
engine.unreal.s1: Import the FBX files into the Content Browser with Combine Meshes turned off, so every model stays a separate mesh.
engine.unreal.s2: Import the palette texture and create one material from it, plus material instances if you want color variations.
engine.unreal.s3: Assign that material to all imported meshes and drag them into your level. They come in at real-world scale.
engine.unreal.s4: Use instanced static meshes or the Foliage tool for repeated props. Nanite is optional, the meshes are already light.
engine.blender.title: Low Poly 3D Models for Blender
engine.blender.how: Open the included .blend file: every model is already marked as an Asset, so the whole pack shows up in Blender’s Asset Browser, ready to drag into your scenes and renders.
engine.blender.s1: Open the included .blend file, or bring the models into your own project with File › Append.
engine.blender.s2: Open the Asset Browser: every model is already marked as an asset, ready to drag into your scene.
engine.blender.s3: The models share one palette material, so editing the palette image recolors the whole pack at once.
engine.blender.s4: Render with Eevee or Cycles, or export your scene to GLB or FBX for any game engine.

faq.title: FAQ: Buying, Licenses & Selling on GameAssets.tr
faq.description: Answers about GameAssets.tr: how buying works, who sets the license, which engines are supported, free assets and how creators list their packs for free.
faq.lead: Still stuck? Reach us on X.
faq.1.a: A free showcase for game assets made by independent studios and artists: 3D models, 2D art, UI, audio, VFX, shaders, fonts and tools. We list the packs; you buy them straight from the creator.
faq.2.q: How do I buy a pack?
faq.2.a: Press Buy on any pack and the creator’s official checkout opens. Pay with card or PayPal; the download is ready at once and stays in your purchase library, including later updates.
faq.3.a: Each creator. The license is in the pack description and in the download. HanX Games packs come with a royalty-free commercial license, explained on the License page.
faq.4.a: It depends on the pack: most work in Unity, Godot, Unreal Engine and Blender. Check the formats and engines in each pack’s description.
faq.5.a: Yes. Use the Free filter on any category, or the “Free to grab” row on the home page.
faq.6.q: I make assets. How do I list them?
faq.6.a: Create a free account, connect your store and import your packs with one link each. Listing is free, with no commission. See the Sell assets page.
faq.7.a: Most popular counts page views, Most bought counts clicks on Buy buttons, and the asset and creator of the week use the last seven days.
faq.8.q: Was generative AI used to make the HanX Games packs?
faq.8.a: No. Every HanX Games model is hand-made. Other creators state how their assets were made in their own descriptions.
faq.9.q: How do I report a problem with a pack?
faq.9.a: Contact the creator through their store page about downloads and files. For stolen content or a broken listing, message us on X (@Hanxgames_) and we review it.
lic.title: Asset Licenses: How Licensing Works on GameAssets.tr
lic.description: Every creator sets the license for their packs. HanX Games packs use a royalty-free commercial license: unlimited games, apps and videos, no attribution required.
lic.lead: Creators set the license for their own packs; you will find it in the pack description and in the download. HanX Games packs use the license below.
lic.canA: Use the assets in unlimited personal and commercial projects: games, apps, videos, client work, game jams and prototypes. Modify, recolour and combine them freely, and ship them inside packaged games on any store. Credit is welcome, never required.
lic.cantA: Resell or redistribute the raw asset files, alone or inside another asset pack, upload them to model libraries or marketplaces, or claim the original models as your own artwork.
lic.unsureA: Ask the creator through their store page. For HanX Games packs, message us on X.
about.title: About GameAssets.tr: a Free Showcase for Game Asset Creators
about.description: GameAssets.tr is a free showcase where independent creators list game assets and developers find them in one place. Run by HanX Games, an indie studio from Türkiye.
about.h1: A shop window for indie asset makers.
about.lead: GameAssets.tr gathers game assets from independent creators in one place.
about.p1: Good assets are scattered across hundreds of store pages, and small creators are hard to find. We built one shop window where 3D models, pixel art, UI, music and tools sit side by side, sorted by category and ranked by what developers actually look at.
about.p2: Listing is free for creators and there is no commission: every purchase happens on the creator’s own store page, so the money goes straight to them.
about.p3: GameAssets.tr is run by HanX Games, an independent game studio from Türkiye, whose own {packs} hand-made packs were the first on the shelf.
